_why: Every defect in that ADR was a constant that read plausibly. That is the
hardest kind of thing to keep fixed, because the wrong version does not
look wrong -- 1e-6 is a perfectly reasonable-looking step and 'negligible
below 1e-6' is a perfectly reasonable-looking threshold. The only thing
standing between this module and a quiet return to all three is whether
the tests added alongside them actually fire. So each mutation here
restores one of the original defects EXACTLY, and asks the harness.
M6 is the interesting one and it is why the continuation tests exist at
all. Branch-following cannot be violated through `analyse`: every model
with more than one branch is refused at the base point, so no perturbed
evaluation ever has a second branch to jump to. Written only against
`analyse`, the guarantee would have been decorative -- true, unreachable,

M6 WAS REPLACED ONCE, and the first version's NOT CAUGHT verdict was correct rather than a test failure: keeping extra_starts and adding global starts back cannot change the answer, because extra_starts are prepended and points[0] is returned. Worth knowing as a property of the implementation -- the anchor wins by position, not by luck -- and worth recording as the shape of mistake this harness catches.

NOTE ON THE TEST COMMAND: it deliberately omits -q. Under this repo's pytest configuration -q suppresses the final 'N passed' line entirely, and scripts/mutate.py reads that line to establish the suite actually RAN. With -q the harness correctly refused the whole set -- 'the baseline suite did not execute any tests' -- rather than grading twelve mutations against a count it could not see. That refusal is the harness working, and it is the same failure testResults.ts records from the other direction.

RESULT, 2026-09-08: 12 caught, 0 not caught, 0 indeterminate. M1-M5 and M7-M12 ran as one set against a green 91-test baseline. M6 was run on its own afterwards because the mutation it applies -- a continuation that re-searches globally at every perturbed evaluation -- makes the suite take roughly twenty minutes rather than ninety seconds. That slowdown is not an inconvenience to work around; it IS the performance half of the decision, reproduced. It is also why the first draft of this module never finished a cascade ranking.

mutations.description: the step goes back to one fixed 1e-6 for every quantity, ignoring declared precision
mutations._claimed: caught by test_the_two_quantities_do_not_get_the_same_step and by the settling-time floor tests
mutations._note: The original defect. A settling time accurate to 1e-8 differentiated with a 1e-6 step reported S = 0.004 for a parameter 1/kd does not contain.
mutations.find: step = float(step) if step is not None else step_for(precision)
mutations.replace: step = float(step) if step is not None else 1e-6

mutations.description: the noise floor is the precision itself rather than precision ** (2/3)
mutations._note: Makes the floor far too fine -- 1e-8 instead of 5e-5 for the settling time -- so method noise reads as signal again.

mutations.description: the dominance test drops the resolution slack, so an exact |S| = 1 is decided by rounding
mutations._note: The coin-flip defect: ks at +0.9999999999621 not dominant, kd at -1.0000000000510 dominant, same model and same true answer.

mutations.description: the two thresholds are re-conflated: negligible means below the arithmetic's floor again
mutations._note: This is the conflation that hid the cascade's real 1e-8 sensitivities behind the words 'no measurable influence'.

mutations.description: the steady-state search drops back below the analysis module's measured default
mutations._note: At 4 the toggle switch reports ONE stable state when it has two, so the multistability refusal never fires and a derivative is taken through a bistable system in silence.

mutations.description: the continuation ignores its anchor and re-searches globally, so it may return a different branch
mutations._note: REPLACED after the first attempt came back NOT CAUGHT, and the harness was right. That attempt kept extra_starts=[anchor] and merely re-enabled the global search alongside it -- which is INERT, because extra_starts are prepended and _continue_from returns points[0], so the anchor's branch converges first and wins no matter how many other starts follow. An inert mutation reads exactly like an untested claim (ADR 0167, F2). This version removes the anchor, which is the actual defect: a continuation that re-decides which branch to be on at every step. Unreachable through analyse -- multistable models refuse at the base point -- which is why TestContinuationStaysOnOneBranch drives follow() directly.

mutations.description: a search with no starting points reports 'no steady states' instead of refusing
mutations._note: A model with no steady state and a search that looked nowhere would then render identically, which is the specific silent lie the check exists for.

mutations.description: an explicit start of the wrong length is padded instead of refused
zero starts per species still generates the floor of four, so a continuation can jump branches
the influence column collapses every negligible row to one word again, discarding the spread
mutations._note: The cascade's twelve constants span four orders of magnitude and that spread IS the ranking. 'negligible here' for all twelve is true and useless.

mutations.description: the default ranking target goes back to the last product of the last reaction
mutations._note: For a cascade that is the DEPHOSPHORYLATED form -- the last reaction of the last tier is the phosphatase step -- so the whole table gets ranked against the opposite of the question.

mutations.description: the table always says 'measure the top of this list', even when nothing on it is worth measuring
